name: Bartram's Ginkgo

location.address: Bartram's Garden, 5400 Lindbergh Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19143 (east of the Bartram Barn)

access: Free, open to visitors every day, grounds open dawn to dusk (Welcome Center Thu-Mon 9:30am-4:30pm). Bartram's Garden is a city-owned public garden and National Historic Landmark; no ticket needed.
transport: Woodland Ave trolley (route 34) to 54th St, then about a 10 minute walk; SEPTA bus routes 12/64 also serve Lindbergh Blvd near the garden entrance
verify_notes: Believed to be the oldest ginkgo in North America: one of three original ginkgoes sent to the US from London in 1785 by William Hamilton of The Woodlands (see phl_004+), who gave one to William Bartram and planted two at his own estate. Hamilton's two at The Woodlands were cut down in the 1980s; this is the survivor. Male tree (ginkgoes are dioecious). Age estimate derived from the 1785 planting date (verify_notes basis, not a bridge claim: both Wikipedia and the garden's own institutional history independently state this specific tree was the one given to Bartram in 1785, not merely that the species arrived that year). Location is approximate: no tree-level coordinates published; text says it stands 'east of the Bartram Barn' within the 45-acre grounds. Wikipedia and the garden's own site agree closely on the facts (both likely draw on the same institutional history), so treat as strong but not fully independent corroboration; flagged for that reason rather than for doubt about the facts themselves. Girth not found this pass.
